name: American Civil War
hook: America's deadliest war: the battles, generals and photographs Jeopardy keeps returning to.

facts.label: Fort Sumter
facts.statement: The war began with the Confederate capture of Fort Sumter in Charleston harbor in April 1861; the fort saw the war's first fatality.

facts.label: Antietam
facts.statement: Antietam, also called Sharpsburg, was the bloodiest single day: over 22,000 killed or wounded on September 17, 1862.

facts.label: Gettysburg
facts.statement: At Gettysburg in July 1863, Joshua Chamberlain held Little Round Top; Lincoln's address there followed that November.

facts.label: Ulysses S. Grant
facts.statement: Grant was made General in Chief in March 1864, during the war; in 1860 he had been working in his father's leather store in Galena, Illinois.

facts.label: Mathew Brady
facts.statement: Mathew Brady organized a photographic corps to document the war, and his battlefield photos are among the first of their kind.

facts.label: Robert E. Lee
facts.statement: When Robert E. Lee left to fight for the Confederacy, the Union turned his family's land into Arlington National Cemetery.

facts.label: Harriet Tubman
facts.statement: Harriet Tubman, the "Moses of Her People," served the Union Army as a cook and nurse during the war.
